My speech at a 10/7 vigil in the Bronx:

Three years ago, October 7th—the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust—cruelly coincided with Simchat Torah.  What should have been a day of joy became one of overwhelming grief, shock, and trauma. On that day, Jews throughout the world were robbed of the joy of Simchat Torah.

When I led a Bronx delegation to Israel for the first time since October 7th, I will never forget the experience of meeting the survivors of the Nova massacre and finding myself inspired by their resilience, by their insistence on defying despair itself, by the message: “We will dance again.” Those words remind us that the joy of Simchat Torah can never be surrendered to terror. It must be reclaimed.  

The most powerful antidote to antisemitism is to be joyfully Jewish.  Franklin Roosevelt once said, “The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.”  Jewish identity is a beautiful gift.  It is not something to be hidden out of fear. It is something to be openly celebrated with joy. With pride. With passion. And with love.

The purpose of terrorism is to strike terror into the heart of a people. The Jewish people and their allies must never stop dancing, never stop singing, and never stop living. Because the moment we stop, terror has won.
And terror can never have the final word on the fate of either the Jewish people or the Jewish State.

So I have a simple call to action:
Never give up. Never give in.
Never stop singing. Never stop dancing.
Relentlessly rejoice in your Judaism.
Am Yisrael Chai.
